SRV-FIX-443 introduced this and it is deliberately ON the lane strand: it is the non-blocking half of the kill grace. It is in the derived set only because it reaches reapLeader_, whose waitpid carries WNOHANG and returns at once. The derivation is transitive by design and must not be narrowed to exclude it; the site is recorded here instead, which is what this file is for.

notes.blocking-primitive-in-app|app/catalog/id: SRV-FIX-532. The wait between attempts on the id ledger's O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock, which is an exclusion between two SERVER PROCESSES — no in-process primitive reaches them and a mutex is forbidden here besides. It runs inside `allocate`'s queue_.offload, on a core::Worker, never on a handler thread, and it is bounded: LOCK_TRIES x LOCK_WAIT_US, after which E26 refuses rather than guessing. Verified at the call site, not assumed.

notes.blocking-primitive-in-app|app/lane/git.c: exec_'s blocking wait on the child it forked, reached only from a core::Worker; and reapLeader_'s WNOHANG wait, which does not block and is what makes the stepped kill grace safe on the strand. SRV-FIX-532 adds the third: spawnConfined waits for the child's exec through an FD_CLOEXEC pipe, and reaps the child ONLY on the path where the exec failed — a process that is already gone, so the wait returns at once and nothing is held. It runs on the same Worker as the spawn it belongs to.
